prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production transparent sprite atlas for Crownforge, a detailed hand-painted isometric medieval woodland strategy game. Create exactly 16 separate full-body sprites of ONE enormous powerful realistic grizzly bear, arranged on an exact 4-column by 4-row evenly spaced grid, true transparent RGBA background with alpha-zero empty space. No labels, text, grid lines, scenery, ground plates, cast shadows or checkerboard. Each cell shows one complete bear with large consistent padding and no overlap. Same brown grizzly individual in all 16 cells: massive muscular shoulders with characteristic high hump, shaggy layered russet-brown fur with warm tawny tips, darker legs, rounded ears, long pale claws, broad muzzle, dark nose. Anatomically convincing bear on four legs, not a wolf, not a monster, no armor or accessories. Polished painted realistic game art, crisp fur masses and readable silhouette, high detail that holds up when zoomed, warm upper-left light, subdued woodland palette. Camera fixed at an elevated isometric 30-degree downward view, orthographic. ROW 1: bear facing screen down-right (southeast, see face and right flank). ROW 2: bear facing screen down-left (southwest, see face and left flank). ROW 3: bear facing screen up-right (northeast, see back and right flank). ROW 4: bear facing screen up-left (northwest, see back and left flank). Each row has the same direction across all four columns. COLUMN 1: weight planted on all four paws, neutral ready stance. COLUMN 2: walk stride with left foreleg advanced and diagonal rear leg following. COLUMN 3: opposite walk stride, right foreleg advanced. COLUMN 4: ferocious low forward paw swipe with one forepaw extended and mouth open, hind feet planted, body still mostly horizontal. Keep camera, body proportions and ground contact baseline consistent between the columns. Uniform body scale across cells. Each row occupies exactly one quarter of canvas height, each column exactly one quarter width. The body must remain entirely inside its own cell including paws, fur, claws and ears. The finished deliverable is just this clean transparent game sprite atlas, ideally 2048 by 2048.
note: Original generated RGBA bytes copied without alteration. Canvas runtime uses measured cell bounds and prepared detail levels.
